items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: and Valery is sitting next to me and he’s just laughing his butt off.

ctx.x: They have a thing called jazz for teens. And they have these kids come in, and he is instructing them how to play jazz. And man these kids, I mean they couldn’t have been any more than maybe 14, 15. And the trumpeter was cool. He was the leader, because he had on the nice suit and the nice shiny shoes and the little handkerchief in his pocket and had his hair all slicked back, had his horn. And he was leading them man. I mean and they’re playing “Night in Tunisia,” the drummer’s doing the thing, and Valery is…

Valery is hipping them and so I think jazz is going to be okay. It’s never going to be popular like it was in the 30s and 40s. You’re never going to see that again. That’s gone, that’s done. But it’s going to be there. If you want to see it, and you know where to find it, you will find it, because it will be there. And we have all these programs still, you have all these colleges with jazz happening in them. You have master’s degrees in jazz history now so that those people will be out there. So I think it’s in…
